# slate-kv-ffi

[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20OR%20Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](#license)

**The stable C ABI for [SLATE](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate).** A `cdylib` + `staticlib` over [`slate-kv`](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/tree/main/crates/slate-kv), with `slate.h` generated by cbindgen at build time. Every non-Rust integration — the [Go binding](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/tree/main/bind/go) and any future one — sits on this surface.

**Not published to crates.io** (`publish = false`): it is a build artifact, not a dependency. You link the library; you do not `cargo add` it.

The ABI surface is specified in [`../../docs/specification.md`](../../docs/specification.md) § 5.8.

## Build

```sh
make ffi-staticlib          # cargo build -p slate-kv-ffi --release
```

Produces:

| Artifact       | Path                                            |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Header         | `crates/slate-kv-ffi/include/slate.h`           |
| Static library | `target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.a`              |
| Shared library | `target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.{so,dylib,dll}` |

`slate.h` is **generated** — `build.rs` rewrites it on every build from the Rust signatures and doc comments. Edit the Rust, never the header.

Rust static libraries do not bundle system libraries, so a static link needs the platform's link flags. Ask the toolchain rather than guessing:

```sh
make ffi-native-libs        # prints the exact --print native-static-libs output
```

Typical results: macOS `-liconv -lSystem -lc -lm`; Linux/glibc `-lgcc_s -lutil -lrt -lpthread -lm -ldl -lc`.

## Hello world

```c
#include "slate.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void) {
    /* Refuse to run against a header from a different ABI generation. */
    if ((slate_abi_version() >> 16) != SLATE_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR) {
        fprintf(stderr, "slate ABI mismatch\n");
        return 1;
    }

    uint8_t key[32] = {0x42};        /* exactly 32 bytes */
    slate_options opts = {
        .capacity_bytes = 4u * 1024 * 1024,
        .max_keys       = 8192,
        .b_commit       = 0,         /* 0 => auto: the scheduler picks B */
        .theta          = 16384,     /* accepted, but see the note below */
        .profile        = SLATE_PROFILE_PI,
    };

    slate_db *db = NULL;
    int rc = slate_open("./slate_db", key, &opts, &db);   /* path is a DIRECTORY */
    if (rc != SLATE_OK) {
        char msg[256];
        slate_last_error_message(NULL, msg, sizeof msg);  /* NULL db => open error */
        fprintf(stderr, "open failed (%d): %s\n", rc, msg);
        return 1;
    }
    memset(key, 0, sizeof key);      /* the engine has derived what it needs */

    slate_put_durable(db, (const uint8_t *)"k1", 2, (const uint8_t *)"v1", 2);

    /* Two-call sizing pattern; see below. */
    size_t len = 0;
    if (slate_get(db, (const uint8_t *)"k1", 2, NULL, &len)
            == SLATE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL) {
        uint8_t *buf = malloc(len);
        if (slate_get(db, (const uint8_t *)"k1", 2, buf, &len) == SLATE_OK) {
            printf("%.*s\n", (int)len, buf);
        }
        free(buf);
    }

    slate_close(db);                 /* best-effort commit, then frees the handle */
    return 0;
}
```

Compile and link:

```sh
# Substitute the flags printed by `make ffi-native-libs` for <native-libs>.
cc example.c -Icrates/slate-kv-ffi/include \
   target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.a <native-libs> -o example
```

## API

| Function                                            | Notes                                                                                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `uint32_t slate_abi_version(void)`                  | `(major << 16) \| minor`. Check before anything else.                                                                                       |
| `int32_t slate_open(path, key, opts, out)`          | `path` is a directory; `key` is exactly 32 bytes, read unconditionally. Writes the handle to `*out`, which is set to `NULL` first.          |
| `int32_t slate_put(db, k, klen, v, vlen)`           | Buffered. **Not durable yet.**                                                                                                              |
| `int32_t slate_put_durable(db, k, klen, v, vlen)`   | Put + commit. Durable on return.                                                                                                            |
| `int32_t slate_get(db, k, klen, v_out, vlen_inout)` | See the two-call pattern below.                                                                                                             |
| `int32_t slate_delete(db, k, klen)`                 | Buffered, like `slate_put`. Follow with `slate_commit` for durability.                                                                      |
| `int32_t slate_commit(db)`                          | The acknowledgement point.                                                                                                                  |
| `int32_t slate_compact(db)`                         | One GC pass.                                                                                                                                |
| `int32_t slate_security_mode(db)`                   | `0` = Full, `1` = BestEffortRollback, `2` = NoRollbackProtection, `-1` = error.                                                             |
| `int32_t slate_close(db)`                           | Best-effort commit, then frees. The handle is dangling afterwards.                                                                          |
| `size_t slate_last_error_message(db, buf, len)`     | NUL-terminated detail for the last failure; returns bytes copied excluding the terminator. Pass `db = NULL` to read a `slate_open` failure. |

The C surface is deliberately narrower than the Rust one. Not exposed: `seal_epoch`, `scrub`, `stats`, `mount_report`, `len`, `epoch`, `acked_seq`, key sources other than raw bytes, and the `durability` option (the ABI always uses `Durability::Full`).

### `slate_options`

```c
typedef struct slate_options {
  uint64_t capacity_bytes;   /* must be <= UINT32_MAX, else SLATE_ERR_INVALID_ARG */
  uint32_t max_keys;         /* index capacity; rounded up, floor 2048 buckets */
  uint32_t b_commit;         /* 0 => auto_b: the scheduler computes B */
  uint32_t theta;            /* accepted but NOT APPLIED at this revision */
  uint8_t  profile;          /* SLATE_PROFILE_PI or SLATE_PROFILE_ESP32 */
} slate_options;
```

Two behaviours worth knowing: `b_commit = 0` is what turns on automatic batch sizing, and **`theta` is currently ignored** — `slate_open` does not forward it, so the engine's compile-time `THETA` = 16,384 applies whatever you pass. `staleness_budget_ms` is fixed at 1000 on this path.

### Return codes

| Code                         | Value | Meaning                                                                    |
|------------------------------|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `SLATE_OK`                   | 0     | Success                                                                    |
| `SLATE_ERR_NOT_FOUND`        | -1    | Key absent (a normal result, not a failure)                                |
| `SLATE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` | -2    | `*vlen_inout` now holds the size you need                                  |
| `SLATE_ERR_INVALID_ARG`      | -3    | NULL pointer, `klen == 0`, oversized key/value, capacity over `UINT32_MAX` |
| `SLATE_ERR_TAMPERED`         | -10   | **The stored data was altered**                                            |
| `SLATE_ERR_ROLLBACK`         | -11   | **An older database image was substituted**                                |
| `SLATE_ERR_INTERNAL`         | -99   | A panic was caught at the boundary                                         |
| `SLATE_ERR_IO`               | -100  | Underlying I/O failure                                                     |

`-10` and `-11` must reach a human. They are not retryable, and a binding that maps them onto a generic error type has removed the feature people chose SLATE for. Note that a **wrong key also surfaces as `SLATE_ERR_TAMPERED`**: an authenticated store cannot distinguish "wrong key" from "altered data".

### The `slate_get` two-call pattern

```c
size_t len = 0;
int rc = slate_get(db, k, klen, NULL, &len);      /* 1. ask for the size  */
if (rc == SLATE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL) {
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(len);
    rc = slate_get(db, k, klen, buf, &len);       /* 2. fetch into it     */
    /* ... */
    free(buf);
}
```

`vlen_inout` is in/out: on entry your buffer's capacity, on return the value's true length — set even when the buffer was too small, which is what makes the sizing call work. `SLATE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` leaves nothing written. A zero-length value returns `SLATE_OK` with `*vlen_inout == 0`.

Ownership is simple by construction: **the library never allocates memory the caller must free.** Values are copied into your buffer; the only owned object is the `slate_db *`, released by `slate_close`.

## Boundary guarantees

- **No unwinding across the ABI.** Every entry point wraps its body in `catch_unwind`; a panic becomes `SLATE_ERR_INTERNAL`.
- **NULL is checked, not assumed.** Every pointer argument is validated before use; a bad one returns `SLATE_ERR_INVALID_ARG`.
- **Bytes, not strings.** Keys and values are arbitrary bytes with explicit lengths, never NUL-terminated. Only `path` is a C string, and it must be valid UTF-8.
- **Errors are per-handle.** Each `slate_db` owns a mutex-guarded last-error string, so two threads on two handles cannot clobber each other's message. Open-time failures use a thread-local, which is why `slate_last_error_message(NULL, …)` is the right call there — and why you must read it on the same thread that failed.

Caller obligations no signature can express: never pass a NULL pointer with a nonzero length, never use a handle after `slate_close`, and serialise calls on one handle under your own lock. (`Db` is internally mutex-guarded, so concurrent calls are memory-safe, but they contend and their ordering is not yours to predict.)

## Testing

```sh
cc crates/slate-kv-ffi/tests/ffi_smoke.c -Icrates/slate-kv-ffi/include \
   target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.a <native-libs> -o /tmp/ffi_smoke && /tmp/ffi_smoke

make bind-test      # runs the Go binding's conformance suite against this library
```

`ffi_smoke.c` covers the ABI check, a rejected oversized-capacity open, the security mode, empty keys and values, the buffer-too-small path, and the reopen-after-close cycle.

## Writing a new binding

Read [`bind/README.md`](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/blob/main/bind/README.md) for the rules every binding follows and [`bind/CONFORMANCE.md`](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/blob/main/bind/CONFORMANCE.md) for the suite it must pass. In short: stay a thin translation layer, derive constants from the generated header, verify `slate_abi_version()` on open, and keep tamper and rollback as distinct types in the host language.
